On the night of Ramchandra Ray's escape, Udayaditya is the one in control, disarming and tying Sitaram up at Sitaram's request; however, on the night of Udayaditya's own escape, Sitaram takes charge by grabbing Udayaditya to lead him out of the prison and providing guidance when Udayaditya asks him where to go.

Pratapaditya's initial, failed plan was to have two Pathan men kill Basanta Ray when he took shelter at the inn in Simultali on his way to Jessore; his life was finally ended by Abdul, who used a drawn sword.

The Mahishi sent Matangini to secretly fetch medicine from Mangala, who prepared a poison intended to ensure that the Yubaraj would feel no pity when Surma died.

Because Rammohan returned alone, the king felt insulted and, unable to take revenge on Pratapaditya or Vibha, decided to take another wife; consequently, when Vibha finally arrived at the palace, she discovered the king was getting married, which shattered her hopes of happiness.

Udayaditya's ring, which had a seal with his name engraved on it, was used to stamp a forged petition that falsely accused the Yubaraj of treason against Pratapaditya; when this petition was presented to Pratapaditya, he ordered Udayaditya's imprisonment.

The dismissal of Sitaram and Bhagavat led Udayaditya to provide them with monthly stipends. Surma then arranged for secret stipends to be sent to the families of the dismissed guards through a trusted maid; when Pratapaditya discovered these secret stipends, he ordered Surma to be sent to her paternal home.

The emotional significance of the song is that it expresses how what was once present has gone away, leaving only emptiness and no one to answer a call, which results in a loss of joy in singing. Basanta Ray sings it first in Raigarh while gazing at the setting sun and reflecting on the absence of those he used to sing for, and second in Jessore while standing in a silent, dark, and empty room in a desolate household after learning of Udayaditya's imprisonment.
Rukmini informs Pratapaditya that the Yubaraj, Sitaram, and the old king conspired to facilitate the escape, which leads the Maharaja to issue a death sentence for the King of Raigarh.

Pratapaditya's initial reception of Ramchandra was indifferent, characterized by a lack of musical fanfare or the lighting of paths and a calm, dismissive manner during their meeting. In contrast, in Ramchandra's court, Pratapaditya is the target of daily verbal attacks from the courtiers, which the king finds amusing.

Rukmini, having left Raigarh and changed her name to Mangala, lives on the outskirts of Jessore, where she uses tantra, mantra, and medicine to prepare a poison that leads to Surma's death, and she later enters Udayaditya's bedchamber during a storm, dressed in soiled and torn clothes, claiming he ruined her and demanding his love.

Udayaditya's early lament about wishing he had been a common subject rather than the crown prince because he lacked the intellect for ruling culminates when, after being brought before his father as a prisoner, he pleads for release from the throne and takes a formal oath before Ma-Kali that he will never sit on the throne of Jessore, never touch the royal scepter, and never rule even an iota of the kingdom.

Nayanchand, who was tasked with delivering the letter to Jessore, became afraid of what Pratapaditya might do and gave the letter to the Mahishi instead. After Basanta Ray read the letter, he concluded that Ramchandra had written it only out of anger and advised the Mahishi to announce that Ramchandra had requested Vibha be sent to her in-laws' house; consequently, the Mahishi announced to the household that Ramchandra had written a letter requesting that Vibha be sent to her in-laws' house.

Pratapaditya's attempt to block the canal with large logs of Sal wood failed because Rammohan and his followers pulled the boat up and over the logs. Furthermore, the pursuit was delayed because the man sent to fetch a boat stopped to smoke a pipe and wake someone up, and the subsequent scolding of the boat-caller lasted so long that the boat could no longer be caught.

Basanta Ray previously stated that he would leave his sitar behind and would not play it anymore when he left Udayaditya; later, he explains that although the sitar is still there, its "strings have broken, and it can no longer be tuned."

Udayaditya's willingness to intervene has decreased significantly; whereas he formerly involved himself in the affairs of the subjects and would fight against oppression with all his might without considering the consequences, he is now gripped by a blind fear of Pratapaditya. This fear causes him to hesitate in every task, fail to stop officials from beating subjects, refrain from preventing the looting and burning of an estate, and lack the courage to provide financial help to those in hardship, even when he intends to do so.
Sitaram enters Udayaditya's dark prison room during a fire, tells him the prison is on fire, and grabs him to carry him out of the prison.

On the first occasion, Rammohan ties thick, large sheets together to make a huge rope, attaches it to a pillar on the palace roof, climbs down the rope with Ramchandra Ray tied to his back, lowers him into a boat in the canal below, and then jumps down himself. On the second occasion, he lifts the unconscious Vibha, carries her out of the palace, and places her into a palanquin near the gate to return to the boat.

When preparing to receive Ramchandra Ray in Jessore, Vibha was elaborately adorned with eight thick gold bangles and one huge diamond bracelet on each arm, a large nose ring, and hair styled by the Mahishi. In contrast, when seeking him out in Chandradwip, she was dressed as a common woman or beggar-woman and entered the palace like a maidservant.

In his bedchamber, the window is a place where Udayaditya sits to remember Surma, looking at the moonlight, garden, and breeze while wondering how she could stay away. In his prison cell, the window symbolizes hope and liberation; seeing the sky and birds through it makes him believe his cage will one day break and he will be free, whereas moving away from the window makes him see only darkness and forget his potential liberation.

Initially, Sitaram used witty rhymes and playful nicknames like "Subhadra," "Pranpriye," and "Priyatame" to borrow money from Rukmini, while she responded with feigned affection and teasing about interest. The dynamic changed after Udayaditya's imprisonment when Sitaram visited Rukmini to curse and threaten her, which provoked a "demonic curse" and "trembling hatred" within her. The encounter became life-threatening when Sitaram entered her cottage at night to steal her money and found a disheveled, ashen-faced Rukmini who threatened to cremate him and the Yubaraj and then attacked at the floor with a curved blade, forcing him to flee.

Sitaram's strategy began by using loyal commoners and palace servants to set five or six rooms on fire simultaneously and using his men to disrupt firefighting efforts by pouring water where there was no fire, failing to return with water, and breaking water pots. This evolved into a full-fledged cover-up when Sitaram's men set fire to Udayaditya's empty prison cell and Sitaram threw bones, a skull, and Udayaditya's sword into the room. To complete the deception, shouts were staged to claim Udayaditya was screaming inside before Sitaram announced the roof had collapsed and there was no response from him, allowing the rumor to spread that the Yubaraj had died in the fire.

Ramchandra Ray was not grateful to Udayaditya for saving his life; instead, he felt that such an act was bound to happen and that it would have been wrong if it had not occurred. He also believed that Udayaditya's main objective was to save his own sister rather than saving Ramchandra Ray himself. As a result, in his court, he brought up Udayaditya's name to laugh and joke about him.

Vibha secretly went to Surma to have her hair done to her own liking because the Mahishi's styling was unbearable. In Surma's absence, when it is time to braid her hair, Vibha sits quietly as if Surma will come at any moment to braid it for her, but Surma does not come and her hair remains unbraided.
